question: Explain how an investor decides whether it controls an investee under Ind AS 110.
sources: Ind AS 110 Consolidated Financial Statements - control and its assessment

points.label: Three elements of control
points.description: An investor controls an investee only if it has power over the investee, exposure or rights to variable returns from it, and the ability to use its power to affect those returns.
points.basis: Ind AS 110, definition and elements of control

points.label: Power and relevant activities
points.description: Power comes from existing rights giving the current ability to direct the relevant activities, meaning those that significantly affect the investee's returns; it may come from voting rights or contracts.

points.label: Substantive and protective rights
points.description: Only substantive rights (that the holder has the practical ability to exercise) count, including substantive potential voting rights; protective rights that only guard the holder's interests do not give power.
points.basis: Ind AS 110, substantive and protective rights

points.label: Less than a majority of votes
points.description: An investor with under half the votes may still have power, for example through agreements with other holders, contractual rights, or a large holding relative to a widely dispersed group of other holders.
points.basis: Ind AS 110, power with less than a majority of voting rights

points.label: Principal or agent, and reassessment
points.description: A decision-maker acting mainly as an agent for others does not control; control is reassessed whenever facts and circumstances show a change in any of the three elements.
points.basis: Ind AS 110, delegated power and continuous assessment
